name: Burundi
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. claims.title: Foundation under Ntare Rushatsi
claims.summary: By tradition Ntare Rushatsi (Ntare I) founds the dynasty of the Kingdom of Burundi; oral histories credit him with ending a famine and unifying competing centres of power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1680-foundation-under-ntare-rushatsi, claim TL:BDI:event:1680:foundation-under-ntare-rushatsi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Expansion under Ntare IV Rugamba
claims.summary: The kingdom roughly doubles in size under Mwami Ntare IV Rutaganzwa Rugamba; by mid-century its borders broadly match those of present-day Burundi.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1796-expansion-under-ntare-iv-rugamba, claim TL:BDI:event:1796:expansion-under-ntare-iv-rugamba, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First European contact
claims.summary: European explorers and missionaries reach the Lake Tanganyika region for the first time, beginning sustained outside contact with the kingdom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1856-first-european-contact, claim TL:BDI:event:1856:first-european-contact, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Burundi assigned to German East Africa
claims.summary: Burundi is incorporated into German East Africa; Germany rules indirectly through the mwami while establishing military posts over the following years.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1890-burundi-assigned-to-german-east-africa, claim TL:BDI:event:1890:burundi-assigned-to-german-east-africa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Belgian conquest of Urundi
claims.summary: Belgian forces invade Urundi during the First World War, ending German control and beginning Belgian administration of the territory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1916-belgian-conquest-of-urundi, claim TL:BDI:event:1916:belgian-conquest-of-urundi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: League of Nations mandate of Ruanda-Urundi
claims.summary: Belgium receives Ruanda-Urundi as a mandate; rule through Tutsi-favouring indigenous hierarchies deepens ethnic stratification. The mandate became a UN Trust Territory in 1946.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1922-league-of-nations-mandate-of-ruanda-urundi, claim TL:BDI:event:1922:league-of-nations-mandate-of-ruanda-urundi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Prince Louis Rwagasore
claims.summary: Weeks after UPRONA's electoral victory, Prime Minister Prince Louis Rwagasore, the independence hero and son of Mwami Mwambutsa IV, is shot dead; the killing is later traced to rival politicians with foreign involvement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1961-assassination-of-prince-louis-rwagasore, claim TL:BDI:event:1961:assassination-of-prince-louis-rwagasore, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence under the monarchy
claims.summary: Burundi becomes independent from Belgium as a constitutional monarchy under Mwami Mwambutsa IV, separating from Rwanda and retaining its throne.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1962-independence-under-the-monarchy, claim TL:BDI:event:1962:independence-under-the-monarchy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of PM Pierre Ngendandumwe
claims.summary: Hutu prime minister Pierre Ngendandumwe is assassinated, deepening the political crisis that followed independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1965-assassination-of-pm-pierre-ngendandumwe, claim TL:BDI:event:1965:assassination-of-pm-pierre-ngendandumwe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Failed Hutu coup and reprisals
claims.summary: A Hutu-led coup attempt fails and is followed by army reprisals, foreshadowing later cycles of violence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1965-failed-hutu-coup-and-reprisals, claim TL:BDI:event:1965:failed-hutu-coup-and-reprisals, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Monarchy abolished; republic declared
claims.summary: Mwami Mwambutsa IV is deposed in July; his son reigns briefly as Ntare V before Captain Michel Micombero overthrows him in November, abolishes the monarchy and proclaims a republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1966-monarchy-abolished-republic-declared, claim TL:BDI:event:1966:monarchy-abolished-republic-declared, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Micombero's military republic
claims.summary: Michel Micombero installs a Tutsi-dominated military republic, concentrating power in the army and state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1966-micombero-s-military-republic, claim TL:BDI:event:1966:micombero-s-military-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Insurrection and the killing of Ntare V
claims.summary: A Hutu-led insurrection erupts in southern Burundi; on 29 April the deposed king Ntare V is killed in Gitega, and large-scale state reprisals begin.

sources.label: The Burundi Killings of 1972
sources.publisher: Sciences Po, Mass Violence and Resistance

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1972-insurrection-and-the-killing-of-ntare-v, claim TL:BDI:event:1972:insurrection-and-the-killing-of-ntare-v, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ikiza mass killings
claims.summary: State and army reprisals kill an estimated 100,000–300,000 people, overwhelmingly Hutu, with educated Hutu deliberately targeted; many scholars regard the events as a genocide. Hundreds of thousands flee abroad.

sources.label: The Burundi Killings of 1972
sources.publisher: Sciences Po, Mass Violence and Resistance

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1972-the-ikiza-mass-killings, claim TL:BDI:event:1972:the-ikiza-mass-killings, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bagaza seizes power
claims.summary: Colonel Jean-Baptiste Bagaza overthrows Micombero in a bloodless coup and pursues limited liberalisation through the late 1970s and early 1980s.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1976-bagaza-seizes-power, claim TL:BDI:event:1976:bagaza-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Buyoya takes power
claims.summary: Major Pierre Buyoya deposes Bagaza in a bloodless coup, becoming president and later steering the country toward reform.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1987-buyoya-takes-power, claim TL:BDI:event:1987:buyoya-takes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ntega and Marangara killings
claims.summary: Ethnic violence in the northern communes of Ntega and Marangara kills thousands, pressuring Buyoya to begin national reconciliation and democratisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1988-ntega-and-marangara-killings, claim TL:BDI:event:1988:ntega-and-marangara-killings, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Multiparty constitution
claims.summary: A new constitution approved by referendum and promulgated in 1992 opens the way to multiparty competition under President Buyoya.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1992-multiparty-constitution, claim TL:BDI:event:1992:multiparty-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ndadaye elected first Hutu president
claims.summary: Melchior Ndadaye of FRODEBU defeats Buyoya to become Burundi's first democratically elected and first Hutu head of state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1993-ndadaye-elected-first-hutu-president, claim TL:BDI:event:1993:ndadaye-elected-first-hutu-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Ndadaye; civil war begins
claims.summary: Ndadaye is assassinated by soldiers after months in office, igniting reciprocal massacres and a civil war that would kill an estimated 300,000 people.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-1993-assassination-of-ndadaye-civil-war-begins, claim TL:BDI:event:1993:assassination-of-ndadaye-civil-war-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arusha Peace Agreement
claims.summary: The Arusha Peace and Reconciliation Agreement, mediated by Nyerere and then Mandela, sets out ethnic power-sharing and a path out of the war.

sources.label: Burundi: Why the Arusha Accords are Central

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-2000-arusha-peace-agreement, claim TL:BDI:event:2000:arusha-peace-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: CNDD-FDD joins the peace process
claims.summary: The main rebel movement, the CNDD-FDD, agrees to the peace process and ceasefires; the war winds down toward the 2005 transition.

sources.label: Burundi: Why the Arusha Accords are Central

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-2003-cndd-fdd-joins-the-peace-process, claim TL:BDI:event:2003:cndd-fdd-joins-the-peace-process, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: CNDD-FDD wins power; Nkurunziza president
claims.summary: Following the Arusha settlement, the former rebel CNDD-FDD wins the 2005 elections and Pierre Nkurunziza becomes president.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-2005-cndd-fdd-wins-power-nkurunziza-president, claim TL:BDI:event:2005:cndd-fdd-wins-power-nkurunziza-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Third-term crisis
claims.summary: Nkurunziza's bid for a disputed third term triggers mass protests, a failed May coup and a deadly crackdown; over a thousand are killed and hundreds of thousands flee.

sources.label: Burundi crisis: The legacy of 2015 brings fear for 2020

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-2015-third-term-crisis, claim TL:BDI:event:2015:third-term-crisis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constitutional referendum
claims.summary: A 2018 referendum amends the constitution and resets presidential term limits, potentially allowing Nkurunziza to remain in power until 2034.

sources.label: We Will Beat You to Correct You: Abuses Ahead of Burundi's Constitutional Referendum

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-2018-constitutional-referendum, claim TL:BDI:event:2018:constitutional-referendum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Succession to Ndayishimiye
claims.summary: Nkurunziza declines to run; Évariste Ndayishimiye wins the May 2020 election. Nkurunziza dies on 8 June and Ndayishimiye is sworn in on 18 June 2020.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burundi: From the drum-kingdom of the mwami to a republic forged in grief", terralore.co/country/BDI/chronicle#ev-2020-succession-to-ndayishimiye, claim TL:BDI:event:2020:succession-to-ndayishimiye, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
